title: 1990 AHSME Problem 20
statement: In the figure, \(ABCD\) is a quadrilateral with right angles at \(A\) and \(C.\) Points \(E\) and \(F\) are on \(\overline{AC},\) and \(\overline{DE}\) and \(\overline{BF}\) are perpendicular to \(\overline{AC}.\) If \(AE=3,\) \(DE=5,\) and \(CE=7,\) then \(BF=\)

solutions.text:
Set \(A=(0,0),\) \(E=(3,0),\) \(C=(10,0),\) \(D=(3,-5),\) and \(B=(f,h),\) where \(h=BF.\) Since \(AB\perp AD,\) \[ (f,h)\cdot(3,-5)=0, \] so \(3f=5h.\) Since \(BC\perp DC,\) \[ (f-10,h)\cdot(-7,-5)=0, \] so \(7f+5h=70.\) Substitution gives \(f=7\) and \(h=\frac{21}{5}=4.2.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Use dot products for the right angles at \(A\) and \(C\)
